discussion_comments.comment_body:
The permission limitation is real, but this proposed fix is unsafe for the supported SSH path. The calling process runs in Session 0, while every candidate desktop login is in another session. Preserving errors only for current_session_id would therefore preserve none of those desktop query errors. A failed query/LookupAccountName does not establish that the login belongs to another account; skipping it could report one eligible login when another same-account login was unreadable.

The startup contract requires exactly one active login for the SSH account, so enumeration stays fail-closed when identity cannot be established. Microsoft documents the Query Information permission requirement but does not guarantee that every query failure identifies an unrelated user: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wtsapi32/nf-wtsapi32-wtsquerysessioninformationw

I have added a short source comment explaining this constraint in the local follow-up. The non-elevated native acceptance passes for the supported tested configuration; hosts that cannot enumerate identities remain an explicit limitation. No session-skipping change is planned without evidence that the omitted session is unrelated.

Fixed in 54483789 by removing remote-desktop from the unconditional command allowlist. Windows already dispatches and returns through its earlier compile-gated handler; non-Windows now reaches the existing unknown-command rejection instead of launching a server.

Removing client-side suppression unconditionally regresses plugin priority when this client connects to a v0.9.4 server. That server still sends unfiltered OSC 8 links and relies on the client to suppress native opening while capture is enabled. The updated client now advertises those links to the terminal, allowing native clicks to bypass an enabled plugin handler. This is a normal upgrade path: `herdr update` leaves generation-1 servers running, and the endpoint handshake still accepts them.

Please advertise server-side selective filtering as an optional endpoint capability and retain the previous capture-enabled suppression when it is absent. A mixed-version regression test should verify that an unfiltered frame from an older server cannot expose plugin-owned links while capture is enabled.

Fixed in 87c4378c. The server advertises `selective_hyperlinks` through the existing optional capability list. The client retains capture-enabled suppression for older compatible servers without it. Capability state is per endpoint, and reconnecting cached surfaces remain protected until the connection is ready. Extended the existing host-terminal playback test using the frozen generation-1 welcome: it failed before the fallback and now passes across current/legacy endpoint switches, upgrades/downgrades, reconnects, capture toggles, full/diff output, and wrapped labels. No frozen codecs or plugin APIs changed. Full native Windows `just check` passed (3,489 Rust tests, 12 existing skips, plus lint/build/scripts/docs).

Addressed in 87c4378c. The optional capability preserves capture-on suppression for older servers, and the playback test covers legacy/current endpoints, switching, and reconnecting cached surfaces. No remaining blocker from this finding.

Fixed in a5d4f5d8. Recovery records no longer use the shared temporary directory. They live under the repository's common Git directory, and old temporary markers are never loaded. Writes use the existing private-file creator (0600 on Unix), create a new temporary file, sync it, and atomically replace the record. Non-file record paths are rejected before writing and ignored when reading. The temporary file is opened with create_new, so an existing symlink is never followed for writing. Record contents are a checked directory identity, not a Boolean lease.

Fixed in f2cb4e75. Herdr now reads the post-close sequence before checking the owner. A writer changing the clipboard between those reads leaves our sampled sequence stale, so the next comparison fails closed; a different owner already present at the check clears the record. This removes the reported owner-then-sequence attribution window without another clipboard read.

Fixed in 3578d13b. The fallback now tightens a parent directory only when it lies inside Herdr's own config/state tree; for an overridden socket path elsewhere it accepts an already owner-only directory and otherwise fails startup with guidance, leaving the directory's permissions unchanged. Verified live on a virtiofs-class mount: default config-tree sockets still start with the directory tightened to 700, while HERDR_SOCKET_PATH pointing into a shared 755 directory now fails cleanly and the directory stays 755. Added unit tests for both the owned-tree and external-directory paths.

Not applicable — `interprocess` already normalizes this. `set_socket_mode` in `interprocess-2.4.2/src/os/unix/c_wrappers.rs:138-145` calls `fchmod()` on the socket descriptor and converts an `EINVAL` result to `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` before returning it, so the `EINVAL` this reports can never reach the match. Matching `Unsupported` is the complete condition; adding `InvalidInput` would widen the fallback to unrelated failures.

The design also changed in the latest head, which makes this moot: permissions are applied to the socket descriptor before `bind()`, so the socket pathname is never chmod()ed and the filesystem in #3212 is never asked to. `private_socket_keeps_other_creation_errors_fatal` now pins that any non-`Unsupported` error stays fatal.

Good catch, fixed in `61f7c7f3`. The unconditional `remove_file` was weaker than what `master` did at the bridge call site, which removed the socket only when its identity still matched (`remove_socket_file_if_owned`).

The fallback now captures the bound socket's `(dev, ino)` immediately after bind and unlinks the pathname only while that identity still holds, so a substituted pathname is left in place and the permission error still propagates. `restriction_failure_leaves_a_replaced_pathname_alone` covers the replacement case; `private_socket_is_removed_when_post_bind_restriction_fails` covers the normal one.

Correcting the auto-applied "Addressed in commit 61f7c7f" marker: `61f7c7f3` did **not** address this. It fixed a different thing on the same lines (identity-checked cleanup when the restriction fails). The bind-then-restrict window you describe is still there on platforms that report `Unsupported`, and that is deliberate. Flagging it so a later reader is not misled by the marker.

The finding is an accurate description of the code, but it is pre-existing behavior, not something this PR introduces:

- On `master`, all four listener sites bound the socket and *then* applied `0600`, on every platform. That window exists in the shipped code today.
- This PR closes it on Linux, where the mode is applied to the descriptor before `bind()`. On platforms where the kernel rejects that (macOS returns `EINVAL`, which `interprocess` maps to `Unsupported`) it leaves the window exactly as it is on `master`. Strictly an improvement, never a regression.

On the two suggested remedies:

- **Fail closed on `Unsupported`** would stop `herdr server` from starting on macOS at all, since macOS takes that branch for every listener.
- **Require a verified private parent before binding** is what an earlier head of this PR did. It was reverted because it regressed macOS in measurable ways: `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` into any non-owner-only directory failed startup, including `/var/tmp` — the workaround documented in #3212; the socket file itself went from `0600` to `0755`; and Herdr chmod'ed the user's config directory to `0700` on every start. That is a poor trade for a local same-host race that `master` already carries.

Hardening the fallback window on macOS is worth doing, but as its own change with its own reasoning about external socket directories — not folded into a virtiofs startup fix. Leaving it out of scope here.
